turns.t: G'day. Um, I'm bloated. Like permanently. And windy. It's been weeks. I think.
How many weeks, would you say?
Oh, I don't know. Maybe, hang on, I wrote it down. Anyway, a few weeks. Or longer. I can't pin the start.
That's fine. Is it there all day, or after certain foods?
By the afternoon, it's like I've swallowed a football. Better in the morning.
Any weight loss, or change in your appetite?
No. Weight's the same. Appetite's fine.
Any blood in your stools, or black stools?
No. No blood.
Any change in your bowels, constipation, looseness? ~
Bit of both, depending on the day. Nothing out of the ordinary for me. ~
Any pain, or vomiting? ~
Some mild cramps now and then. No vomiting. ~
And any trouble with your waterworks, or anything gynaecological, pelvic pain or a change in your periods? ~
No. All normal. ~
Let me press your tummy. Lie back on the couch for me. ~
Sure. Is this going to hurt? ~
Not if I can help it.
Your tummy is soft, and I can feel it's bloated and a little tight, but it's not tender, and I can't feel any lumps.
Is that good? ~
It's what I'd hoped. Any breathlessness, chest pain, or cough?
No, nothing like that.
Right. Bloating that comes on through the day, with a bit of both loose and hard stools, fits with irritable bowel, but I can't rule out something like coeliac disease or lactose intolerance.
How do you find out? ~
Often by keeping a food diary, and trying changes one by one. ~
A food diary, I could try. ~
Write down what you eat, when the bloating comes, and your bowel habits, for two weeks.
Right. And what should I eat? ~
Regular meals, eat slowly, avoid fizzy drinks and chewing gum, and cut down on beans, onions, and sweeteners.
Ah, I do love my sugar-free gum. ~
That could be a culprit, actually. ~
Well, I'll stop that and see. Thanks, doc. ~
Hope it settles. ~

physical_examination.normalized_finding: Soft, bloated, non-tender abdomen without masses

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient could not say when the bloating began ("a few weeks. Or longer. I can't pin the start").

clinical_actions.description: Keep a two-week food and bowel diary
Regular meals, eat slowly, avoid fizzy drinks, gum, beans, onions and sweeteners
